answer.description: A person who has linked Telegram via the connect handshake.

A Telegram message — what a listen delivers, whole: read `e.`Text`` straight off the event, reply along its `Replies` edge. Created only along an edge: DM a linked user via their `Messages` edge, reply via a message's `Replies` edge — the chat and the reply target come from the parent, never from fields.

fields.description: The Telegram message id.
The message text. On an inbound message: the received text (or the media caption; empty for caption-less media). On a send: the message body — required.
The id of the chat the message belongs to — the value to send a reply back to.
private / group / supergroup / channel.
The numeric id of the user who sent the message.
The @username of the sender, when set.
The sender's first name.
When the message was sent (ISO-8601).

references.name: Attachments
references.description: Files attached to the message — documents, photos, voice notes, audio (zero or more).

references.name: Replies
references.description: Send a reply threaded under this message (write-only — the Bot API cannot list replies). The chat and the reply target come from this message.

references.name: Sender
references.description: The linked user who sent this message — resolves only for a sender who completed the connect handshake (private chats); a group chat or an unlinked sender resolves to nothing.

answer.description: A person who linked Telegram via the connect handshake. Their `Chat Id` is the value a send targets (private chat id = user id).

fields.description: The private chat id a send targets (= the Telegram user id).
The Listen-Fire account email this Telegram user linked as.
When the link handshake completed (ISO-8601).

references.name: Messages
references.description: Send a message into this person's private bot chat (write-only — the Bot API cannot list a chat's history). The chat id is the linked user's own id.

fields.description: The Bot API file id — resolves to the file bytes.
